rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures
rawCommits.body:
The published Windows installer was silently failing to launch on
upgraded machines. Symptom: double-click AURA, the harness sidecar
(aura-node-...) appears as a Background process in Task Manager,
and then nothing — no window, no error dialog, no notification.
Only `<localdata>/aura/crash.log` showed evidence of what happened:

  panicked at apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs:106:10:
  server thread failed before becoming ready: RecvError

Root cause is a chain of three bugs that combine into "exits
silently with no UI":

1. `<localdata>/aura/store/settings.json` was a 1.1 MB file of
   pure NUL bytes — a torn-write artifact from a prior crash.
   `SettingsStore::load_cf` handed the bytes to
   `serde_json::from_str`, which propagated `expected value at
   line 1 column 1` straight up. The same store path is read in
   two places: `init_script::load_bootstrapped_auth_literals`
   already swallowed the error and warned, but the
   server-thread path inside `aura-os-desktop` `.expect(...)`'d
   on it and panicked.
2. `persist_cf` wrote the tmp file with `fs::write` and renamed
   it without `sync_all`. NTFS happily renames a file whose
   contents the OS has not yet flushed; a power loss or hard
   kill in that window leaves the destination as the right
   length but full of NUL bytes, which is exactly the input
   that bug 1 chokes on the next time around.
3. The release Windows binary is built with
   `windows_subsystem = "windows"`, so the panic's `eprintln!`
   went to a stderr that has no console. The only surviving
   evidence was `crash.log`, which a non-developer user has no
   reason to look at.

Fixes:

- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::load_cf`: on
  `serde_json::from_str` failure, rename the bad file aside
  to `<cf>.json.corrupt-<unix_ts>`, log a WARN, and return an
  empty CF. Mirrors the per-entry tolerance the same function
  already applies to invalid base64. Two new integration tests
  cover the all-NUL and garbage-JSON shapes.
- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::persist_cf`: replace
  `fs::write` with `OpenOptions::open` + `write_all` + a
  `sync_all` before the rename so the atomic-rename promise
  actually holds across crashes. Costs one fsync per persist.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/net/server.rs::spawn_server`:
  change the ready channel from `()` to `Result<(), String>`
  and stop `.expect`ing on `build_app_state` /
  `TcpListener::from_std`. On failure, log the error and send
  `Err(message)` back so the main thread can react.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs`: handle the new ready
  result. On `Ok(Err(_))` or `RecvError`, call a new
  `init::fatal_dialog::show_fatal_startup_failure` helper
  before exiting non-zero.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/init/fatal_dialog.rs` (new): pop
  a native MessageBoxW with MB_TOPMOST + MB_SETFOREGROUND on
  Windows; fall back to `eprintln!` on macOS / Linux. The
  dialog body names the data dir, the path of the crash log,
  and the corrupt settings file the user can rename to recover.

Verified locally: `cargo test -p aura-os-store` (7 tests, both
new self-heal cases included) and
`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop -- --print-channel` (Channel CI
gate from f64e07753 still passes).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures

rawCommits.subject: fix(memory): read by bare template id, not partition key
rawCommits.body:
The May 7 fix routed memory reads through `${agent_id}::default`,
but the harness keys long-term memory by the bare template id (via
`Session::memory_agent_id`, which derives an `AgentId` from the
billing `aura_agent_id` UUID). Its router's `parse_agent_id` only
accepts UUID / 32-byte hex, so every partitioned memory request
returned 400 and the UI fell back to "no memories yet".

restore the strongly-typed `Path<AgentId>` extractors so a malformed
caller fails at the proxy edge instead of being forwarded as a bad
string, and drop the partition-shaped tests that asserted the wrong
contract (the mock harness happily echoed the partition key while
the real harness was rejecting it).

rawCommits.subject: fix(mode-selector): equal-width segments to stop pill border jitter
rawCommits.body:
The SlidingPills indicator transitions transform, width and height
together when the active mode changes. transform runs on a composited
layer but width / height force a CPU layout + paint each frame, so the
1px accent border lands at slightly different sub-pixel positions on
intermediate frames and reads as a small wobble on the pill outline
during the slide.

Pin every mode segment to the same min-width (56px desktop, 68px on
the mobile breakpoint, both border-box so the value covers padding) so
every segment measures identically. The width / height transitions
then become no-ops on mode changes and only transform actually
animates, which is fully GPU-composited and pixel-stable.

SlidingPills itself is left untouched so any future consumer that
genuinely needs unequal segment widths still gets the size transition.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(agents-chat): decouple wire project_id from picker selection
rawCommits.body:
Introduces an `llmProjectId` prop on `ChatPanel` (forwarded through
`useChatPanelState` as `wireProjectId`) that drives `body.project_id`
on the wire, separately from `selectedProjectId` which still anchors
the picker label and chat-persistence target. Defaults to
`selectedProjectId` so existing callers (projects-app via
`AgentChatPanel`, which now passes `llmProjectId={projectId}`
explicitly) keep their current behavior.

The agents-app side (`useStandaloneAgentChat`) computes
`llmProjectId` so:
- new sessions / fresh canvas / context reset always ship Home;
- existing sessions opened via `/agents/:agentId?session=<id>` ship
  the session-of-record's original project, recovered from
  `sessions-list-store` via the new `findSessionProjectId` helper —
  even when the user lands from a row unrelated to today's selected
  display project;
- legacy agents with no Home binding ship `undefined` and let the
  server's lazy heal in
  `setup_agent_chat_persistence_with_matched` create the binding on
  first turn. A heal-refresh effect then nudges
  `useProjectsListStore.refreshProjects` so the freshly-created Home
  row materializes locally for subsequent sends instead of waiting
  for a hard reload.

Test updates wire matching mocks for
`useProjectsListStore.refreshProjects`,
`useSessionsListStore.{sessionsBySurface, replaceSessionId,
bumpVersion, addOptimisticSession}`,
`agentSessionsSurfaceKey` / `projectSessionsSurfaceKey`, and a
minimal `buildOptimisticSession` shape.

rendered.title: AURA Video debuts, Windows startup self-heals, and the desktop shell gets a chrome refresh
rendered.intro: A dense nightly: a brand-new AURA Video generation app lands end-to-end, the Windows desktop client learns to recover from corrupt settings instead of vanishing, and the desktop shell, taskbar, and chat input bar get a coordinated polish pass. Release infrastructure also got tougher against Apple notary blips and dropped GitHub asset uploads.

entries.title: Invite friends modal and per-panel border tokens
entries.summary: An invite-a-friend entry point lands in the taskbar and the desktop lanes gain their own borderable surfaces.

items.text: Added a pulsing Invite button to the bottom-left taskbar that opens a new modal showing the user's invite code (click to copy) and referral bonus details.

Wrapped the sidebar, main panel, and sidekick lanes in a 1px border so they read as discrete surfaces, and introduced separate `--color-border-main-panel` and `--color-border-chrome` tokens exposed in Settings → Appearance → Custom colors for independent tinting.

entries.title: Release pipeline reconciles dropped GitHub asset uploads
entries.summary: A new retry-and-verify step makes transient upload failures recoverable instead of fatal across every release channel.

items.text: Added `upload-release-assets-with-retry.sh`, wired in after every `softprops/action-gh-release` step on nightly, stable, and mobile-nightly workflows. It diffs local artifacts against the published release and re-uploads only the missing or wrong-sized files via `gh release upload --clobber`, so a single dropped stream from GitHub's upload API no longer reds a 40-minute job.

entries.title: Rounded lanes, unified sidekick width, and onboarding-only prompt chips
entries.summary: Three focused shell changes simplify the desktop layout and trim noise from the chat empty state.

items.text: Replaced the inset divider between the main panel and the sidekick with explicit rounded corners on the sidebar, sidekick lane, and main panel host, with the rounding conditional on sidekick visibility.

Unified the sidekick lane to a single shared width across every app, persisted under one `aura-sidekick-width` key and migrated from the legacy shared / projects / per-app entries so existing users keep their preferred size.
Restricted the empty-thread prompt suggestion chips to onboarding only — they now disappear permanently the moment a user sends their first message.

entries.title: AURA Video app, silent-launch Windows fix, and a taskbar refresh
entries.summary: The day's biggest batch ships a new video generation app, rescues Windows users hit by a corrupt settings file, restores agent memory, and cycles the Earn Credits / theme toggle / Invite button placement across the chrome.

items.text: Diagnosed and fixed the silent-launch failure on upgraded Windows installs: the settings store now renames a corrupt `settings.json` aside and continues with an empty store, persists writes through `sync_all` to prevent torn renames after a crash, propagates server-thread failures instead of `.expect`-panicking, and shows a native 'AURA could not start' MessageBox pointing at the crash log and recovery file.

Introduced AURA Video as a full standalone app: a video generation proxy at `/api/generate/video/stream`, a Zustand store with artifact persistence, three Veo models (Fast, Standard, Lite), and a complete shell with main panel, left nav project tree, sidekick thumbnail gallery, and sidekick taskbar tab.

Restored agent long-term memory reads by reverting the partition-key routing back to the bare agent id the harness actually expects, with strongly-typed `Path<AgentId>` extractors so malformed callers fail at the proxy edge.

Iterated heavily on chrome placement: restyled the Earn Credits button as an accent pill, moved it to the titlebar, reverted it back to the taskbar, floated it at the bottom of the left sidebar, and finally landed it as a compact 'EARN' pill in the titlebar next to the sidekick toggle; the theme toggle moved from the titlebar into the bottom taskbar, and the right cluster now collapses to a profile-only state by default.

Tightened sidebar and selector visuals: inset-pill row highlights with a unified selected color, a chrome-pill PanelSearch with a softer 30%-of-chrome border, fully-tinted accent fills for the active ModeSelector pill (with contrast-aware label color), and equal-width mode segments to eliminate sub-pixel border jitter during the slide animation.

entries.title: macOS packaging retries through Apple notary outages
entries.summary: The macOS release job now treats transient Apple notary errors as flakes instead of build failures.

items.text: Extended the `should_retry_packaging` matcher to recognize `xcrun notarytool` HTTP 429 and 5xx responses in packager.log, so brief Apple notary outages no longer abort the entire macOS packaging job alongside existing hdiutil 'Resource busy' retries.

entries.title: Standalone-agent chat pins to Home and the input bar gets icon-hover plates
entries.summary: Standalone agent chats now consistently target a 'Home' project on the wire while keeping the picker simple, and shared icon buttons adopt a tighter rounded hover plate.

items.text: Standalone Agents-app chats now always show a single non-interactive 'Home' label in the project picker — auto-created Home bindings are used directly, legacy agents get a synthesized 'Home' entry pointing at their existing binding, and a new `llmProjectId` prop decouples the wire `project_id` from the picker so fresh canvases ship Home while existing sessions ship their session-of-record's original project.

Introduced a shared inner-plate hover style for icon buttons driven by new `--icon-hover-inset`, `--icon-hover-radius`, and `--icon-hover-bg` tokens, applied across taskbar icons, the browser address bar, folder picker, onboarding checklist, and the chat input's `+` / send buttons; also added `interface/docs/icon-system.md` as the source-of-truth for icon usage.

Tuned taskbar icon centering and sizing — locking `line-height: 0` and `svg { display: block }` to fix sub-pixel off-center hover halos, then settling the lucide glyph at 16px inside a 30×30 hit target after a brief 19→15→16 iteration.

Polished the chat input bar: dropped the slash hint button in favor of a `/ for commands, @ for context` Code-mode placeholder, aligned the mode pill with the attach button, extended the mode-bar divider to the right edge, and inset the send/new-chat buttons by 2px to match attach for symmetric corners. Sidebar, project tree, sidekick, and sessions list rows also gained a 1px gap so adjacent highlights no longer touch.

highlights: New AURA Video generation app with left nav, sidekick gallery, and Veo models
Windows installer no longer dies silently on a corrupt settings file
Release pipeline reconciles dropped GitHub uploads and retries Apple notary outages
Unified sidekick width, rounded lane corners, and a refreshed icon-hover system
